title: Reading Drill — Improving a station's public clock — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Improving a station's public clock — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The station electrician had been asked to investigate travellers seeing different times at opposite entrances in Hillswick. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the difference between clock readings, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a six-week comparison, the team used timed checks at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because power interruptions might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a shared time signal. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
